summary: Abram cuts the animals down the middle and places their halves opposite each other. The verb names the cut, and the noun names a piece it produces.

senses.definition: To divide into pieces by cutting.

evidence.note: The closing words וְאֶת הַצִפֹּר לֹא בָתָר say that Abram spared the birds the cutting he had performed on the other animals.

senses.definition: To cut through the middle, producing two halves.

evidence.note: בַּתָּוֶךְ specifies where Abram cuts, and each half has a matching half that he places opposite it.

senses.definition: A piece produced by cutting, especially one half of a divided animal.

evidence.note: After the cut through the middle, בִּתְרוֹ denotes the half placed opposite its mate.
The calf is cut in two, and the covenant makers pass between its pieces.
